subject: Azure marketplace private offer — multi-year prepay & ramp milestones
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@atlasdata.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@atlasdata.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Interest in Azure private offer + multi-year prepay options

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the cost transparency you showed. Our procurement and platform teams asked me to follow up about whether Redwood can support a multi-year prepay via Azure Marketplace private offer. A few items they care about: 

- Ability to make an up-front annual prepayment (we'd prefer a single payment per year)
- Tiered discounts for 1/2/3-year terms (we're evaluating 3yr to get the best economics)
- Ramp schedule flexibility (we won't consume evenly year-over-year; Year 1 will be ~30% of projected run rate)
- Performance / SLA credits tied to throughput milestones during ramp
- Marketplace listing & private offer expiration/change window

Can you share how Redwood structures term discounts for marketplace private offers and whether you can map milestone-based credits to the Azure PO? Also please send any term sheet or price illustration so our procurement team can model it.

Attaching our internal ramp model for reference.

Thanks,
Oliver
Senior Platform Engineer
Atlas Dataworks
[Attachment: Atlas_Ramp_Model.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@atlasdata.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T14:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Interest in Azure private offer + multi-year prepay options

Hi Oliver — great to hear, and thanks for the ramp model. Happy to explore a 3-year prepay via Azure Private Offer. High level from our side: 

- We support annual prepay payments through Marketplace private offers (PO can be configured for yearly invoicing or single up-front payment per term).
- Typical economics for Azure PO vs direct invoice: Marketplace takes a platform fee (~3-6%) so list discount needs to account for that to keep net to Redwood consistent.
- For a 3-year structure we often propose a tiered effective discount that increases with term length and higher upfront commitment. Example (illustrative):
  • 1-year prepay: standard 15% list discount
  • 2-year prepay: 20% list discount
  • 3-year prepay: 25% list discount + an additional uplift if >50% paid in year 1
- Ramp/milestones: we can bake in milestone credits (applied as future invoice credits) tied to integration and throughput milestones. We typically map milestone credits to HubSpot/PO and to the private offer so your procurement team sees line-item credits.

I'm attaching a short term sheet and a draft private offer template used for Azure to make modeling easier. If you can confirm target total commit over 3 years (vs the ramp you shared) I can run a scenario with exact numbers and return a proposed private-offer payload for Azure.

Next steps: confirm target 3yr commit (not just projected usage) and whether you need price protection for Year 2/3. I can loop in our marketplace ops and legal for the PO flow once we have those.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[hannah_schmitt@redwood.com]
[Attachment: redwood_3yr_term_sheet_v1.pdf (PDF, 82KB); azure_private_offer_template.docx (DOCX, 24KB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T10:02:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Atlas — Azure PO / 3yr prepay — pricing ask (need approvals)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Atlas request. High level: they like the runtime, want a 3yr private offer via Azure with yearly prepayments. Their internal ramp skews Year1 ~30%, Year2 ~35%, Year3 ~35% (see attached). Procurement will want both list discount and price-protection language.

My proposed commercial starting point (for discuss):
- Total 3yr committed ARR (example): $1,200,000 list
- Structure: Year1 prepay $480,000 (40% of list), Year2 $360,000, Year3 $360,000 (they can pay yearly via marketplace PO)
- Marketplace list discount (applied at offer creation): 22% off list for a 3yr term with year1 upfront >=40%
- Additional milestone credits: up to $30k credit applied if integration & throughput milestone achieved within first 6 months (SLO: sustained 99th p99 latency < 250ms at 100 RPS)
- Price protection: cap list price increases to <=2% year-over-year on the private offer

Questions: are we comfortable with 22% list discount on a 3yr? That nets to Redwood after marketplace fee ~18% effective. Also need guidance from legal/marketplace ops on whether the milestone credit needs a separate credit memo or can be encoded as a line-item allowance on the private offer.

Attaching the draft term sheet and their ramp model.

Thanks — Hannah
[Attachment: redwood_3yr_term_sheet_v1.pdf; Atlas_Ramp_Model.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas — Azure PO / 3yr prepay — pricing ask (need approvals)

Hannah — thanks for the draft. A few comments from pricing/sales: 

- 22% list discount feels OK as a starting offer for a mid-market account with strategic potential, but push them for a larger Year1 upfront (45-50%) to improve our cash profile.
- Keep the milestone credit but convert it to an SLA credit capped monthly (easier for marketplace ops to model). Suggest $10k / quarter applied as credits for missed SLOs or as earned credits for early integration completion.
- Avoid multi-year price-protection guarantees that are absolute — offer a 2% cap but include language that material architectural changes or new feature bundles are out of scope.
- Include a 30-day private-offer change window in the PO for minor adjustments; don't accept open-ended edit windows.

If they insist on more generous economics, get a commitment to a joint case study and logo use for 12 months as concession.

Marissa
VP, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Grant <oliver@atlasdata.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@atlasdata.com, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@atlascloud.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace private offer + multi-year prepay options — counter

Hannah — thanks for the clarity and the term sheet. Procurement reviewed and sent back the following counter-proposals: 

1) Year1 upfront percent: they request 25% upfront (lower than your ask) but want a guarantee that unused credits roll forward within the private offer year rather than expiring.
2) Discount: request 25% list discount on a 3yr if Atlas can commit to a $1.2M total 3yr spend (they propose the same total, but want slightly better economics).
3) Price protection: they ask for a 2% cap, plus a 1% floor (i.e., if we increase list price they get a 1% credit retroactive), they say it's important for budgeting.
4) Milestone credits: they prefer credits paid as a line-item credit within the private offer so it shows on the PO; if that's not possible, credits must be convertible to future usage within 12 months.

I've attached the updated ramp model and a short procurement note. We are OK with a joint case study but would need a legal-approved MVPA first. 

Can you confirm what you can accept/decline so we can move to procurement sign-off?

Regards,
Oliver
[Attachment: Atlas_Ramp_Model.xlsx; Atlas_Procurement_Notes.pdf]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace private offer + multi-year prepay options — counter

Oliver — thanks for the clear counter. Quick responses inline: 

- Year1 upfront: we can accept 25% upfront for Year1 but will require Year1 payment within 30 days of PO activation. Unused prepaid credits can roll forward within the private offer for up to 12 months — we will encode that as a usage allowance on the PO.
- Discount: we can do 25% list discount on the 3yr total of $1.2M provided Atlas signs the private offer and the DocuSign SOW within 30 days. That nets to Redwood after marketplace fee ~20% effective.
- Price protection: 2% cap is acceptable. We can't offer an automatic 1% retroactive credit for price increases, but we can include a one-time reconciliatory credit if pricing changes materially (>3%) and it's agreed by both parties during an annual review.
- Milestone credits: marketplace ops prefers credits as line-item allowance where possible; we'll aim to show a $30k "integration allowance" as a line-item on the Azure private offer, payable as credits or usage allowance up to 12 months. If Marketplace UI blocks this, we'll issue a credit memo applied to future invoices.

Next steps: 
1) I'll draft the private-offer payload and send to Claire at Azure Marketplace ops for validation.
2) Legal will prepare the MVPA and SOW — I'll loop legal once you confirm sign-off on the high-level terms.
3) I'll create the HubSpot opportunity and attach the PO payload + term sheet.

If that all works, can you confirm the $1.2M total and the commit to sign within 30 days? Once confirmed I'll kick off marketplace ops.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
